answer: Weight comes only from grades a key has sealed: each is a quorum-checked verdict written to the ledger with its own quill, and no identity can be handed another's record. A fresh clone starts at the foot of the slope, never the summit; its garden of accrued judgments is bare. To field M sybils an attacker must grade M separate ways up, repeating each epoch's labor per key, so cost rises linearly with the fake count while one warmed, non-transferable credential cannot be shared across them.
